html:
The Beylik of Aydin was a Turkish principality on the Aegean coast of western Anatolia, around Smyrna (now Izmir), from the early 14th century to 1425. It is shown here in 1400. It was one of the Anatolian beyliks that rose as Seljuk and Mongol power faded.

Its founder Mehmed Bey took the region from the Byzantines and ruled from Birgi. His son Umur Bey built a fleet and became a famous sea raider in the Aegean. He also allied with the Byzantine pretender John Kantakouzenos in the civil war of 1341 to 1347.

His raids provoked the Smyrniote crusades: in 1344 a Christian league took the harbour castle of Smyrna, and Umur was killed trying to retake it in 1348. The Ottomans annexed Aydin in 1390. Timur restored it after he crushed the Ottomans at the Battle of Ankara in 1402, but the Ottomans took it back for good in 1425.
